why: The plan is pitched at a lay audience, and sections 2 and 3 lean on plasma, the interplanetary magnetic field and corpuscular radiation without saying what any of them is: a first-time viewer is left holding three words no line explains (structure 8; attention 24, 26; judging 14).
judging_10: judging 10 asks the calibration run to fail the reviewer on every seeded case; this fault is not the story review's to catch. The story here is the good one, and the rubric has no criterion for terms a lay viewer is never given: open_loops' Fair is a question never answered or a setup never paid, which this arc does not have. judging 14 puts unexplained terms in the cold read, among the pre-voice checks that are not story checks. So the story review is read here and not judged, and the calibration fails a cold read that does not list the terms, each by one of the names the case accepts.

review.logline: A comet's tail leads it away from the Sun because sunlight and a wind from the Sun push it, not because it trails behind.
review.synopsis: A comet leaves the Sun tail first; sunlight is too weak to explain the gas tail; Biermann proposes a wind from the Sun and Mariner 2 measures it; the opening comet is seen again.

first_minute.promise_match: The comet and its tail are on screen and named at once.
first_minute.question_and_stakes: Why the tail leads; the same wind reached Quebec in 1989.
first_minute.gap: why a comet leaving the Sun has its tail in front
